issues.display_title: Issue #36: fix(gps): Align total distance, selected frame count and map markers with Electron
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Before

After

Description

Video Info reported 6911 Meter and 72 selected frames for the project Crop, where the Electron app reports 107 Meter and 17 for the same video and the same GPS setting (5 Meter). The map also drew its distance dots away from the blue route line, left the first dot unconnected, and let the dots drift while the map was dragged.

The Electron app is the reference for all of these numbers.

Root Causes

  1. GPS track was never trimmed to the clip. An Insta360 .gpx sidecar covers the whole recording session. For Crop that is 1511 points across 28 minutes (6911 m), while the exported video is 60 seconds. Electron trims the track when it loads it (open.js:315-390): points sharing a timestamp collapse to the middle one, repeated coordinates are skipped, and the walk stops once the second counter passes the clip duration — 61 points, 107 m. The Tauri port loaded all 1511 points.
  2. Total distance was read off the wrong point. Electron assigns totalDistance on every walked coordinate, outside the spacing gate (measure-distance.js:148), so it is the route length at the last walked coordinate. The port used the distance of the last published marker, which stops earlier whenever trailing points fail the gate.
  3. Selected frame count used the published set. Electron shows selectLayer.length — the raw walk entries in GPS mode, the every-nth list in layers mode. The port showed the valid, deduplicated publish set, which is smaller.
  4. Marker coordinates were resolved against the wrong list. KeptPoint.track_index counts the filtered coordinate list in GPS mode, but the IPC layer used it to index the raw track, so the dots landed on unrelated points. The blue line was drawn from the raw track rather than through the markers (Electron's createLinesFromMarkers), and an Insta360 slice(1) left the first dot unconnected.
  5. Marker hover animated transform. MapLibre positions markers with an inline transform, so a CSS transition on that property made every dot lag behind the map while panning.

Changes Made

  • crates/sb-core/src/gps/selection.rs: added prep_insta360() (timestamp grouping, coordinate de-duplication, duration cut-off, second - 1 counter, empty track for clips of 5 s or less) and wired it into load_track() for Insta360 sources; added walk_route_meters() for the Electron totalDistance semantics; KeptPoint now carries its own coordinate.
  • src-tauri/src/commands/projects.rs: markers report their own coordinate; the unused route field was removed from the IPC result.
  • src/features/map/components/MapCanvas.tsx: the route line is built from the markers, with no marker dropped.
  • src/features/map/styles/marker.module.scss: hover uses a box-shadow ring instead of transform: scale().
  • src/features/projects/components/VideoInfoModal.tsx: selected frame count follows selectLayer; feet use Math.floor(m / 0.3048) as convertMetersToFeet does.

Verification

Crop_sb at GPS 5 Meter now computes total_distance=107 markers=17 frames=17, matching Electron. Covered by new unit tests plus the existing Electron golden replay; cargo clippy --workspace, pnpm build, pnpm test and pnpm lint are clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #38: fix(auth): Stop the macOS keychain prompt on every app launch
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Description

macOS asked for keychain access every single time the app was opened, and choosing "Always Allow" did not stop the prompt from coming back on the next launch.

Root Cause

macOS binds a keychain item's ACL to the code signature of the binary that created it. The app binary is ad-hoc, linker-signed:

Identifier=street_builder-c33f1a6708685f89
CodeDirectory ... flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed)
Signature=adhoc
TeamIdentifier=not set

An ad-hoc signature carries no stable identity, so the ACL falls back to the binary's cdhash. Every rebuild produces a new cdhash and a new identifier suffix, so the item stored by the previous build never matches the running one and macOS prompts again. "Always Allow" only ever applied to the build that was running at the time.

Changes Made

  • src-tauri/src/session_store.rs (new): FileSessionStore writes the session (identity + bearer token + expiry) as session.json in the app data dir — ~/Library/Application Support/com.streetbuilder.app/ on macOS — with 0600 permissions. A corrupt file reads as "no session" rather than failing the launch.
  • src-tauri/src/keychain.rs: removed, along with the keyring dependency.
  • src-tauri/src/state.rs: AppState builds the store from app_data_dir.
  • crates/sb-core/src/auth: documentation updated; the SessionStore trait itself is unchanged, so the token still never crosses the IPC boundary.

Trade-off

The token is no longer encrypted at rest. It is protected by file permissions alone, so anyone able to read this account's home directory can read it. This was chosen deliberately over prompting on every launch.

Upgrade Note

Existing users are logged out once and sign in again. The old com.streetbuilder.app keychain entry is no longer read and can be deleted by hand.

Verification

cargo test -p street-builder covers the round trip, clearing twice, the 0600 permission bit, and the corrupt-file path. cargo check -p street-builder and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets are clean.
